description: Designing and building applications that are native to the cloud: cloud-native principles, functions as a service, managed databases and object storage, event-driven design with queues and streams, APIs and gateways, observability of distributed systems, and designing for cost. Practised by building and deploying a complete event-driven application in a simulated cloud console and code editor in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong final-year cloud application development course and the cloud developer certifications.
modelledOn: CNCF Cloud Native Definition and the CloudEvents specification
Hohpe and Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns
AWS Certified Developer - Associate and Microsoft Azure Developer Associate objectives
outcomes: Apply cloud-native principles to design stateless, loosely coupled and resilient applications.
Build, configure and test functions as a service and explain cold starts, concurrency and execution limits.
Choose and model managed databases and storage services for given access patterns and consistency needs.
Design event-driven systems with queues, topics and streams that handle retries, ordering and idempotence correctly.
Expose and secure APIs through gateways and instrument applications with logs, metrics and distributed traces.
Estimate, compare and reduce the cost of serverless and container-based designs.

units.title: Cloud-native principles
topics: What cloud-native means: containers, microservices, declarative APIs, immutable infrastructure, automation
Twelve-factor applications: configuration, backing services, disposability, logs as event streams
Monoliths, modular monoliths, microservices and serverless: when each fits
Designing for failure: timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breakers, bulkheads

units.title: Functions as a service
topics: The FaaS execution model: triggers, handlers, statelessness, ephemeral storage, timeouts and memory settings
Cold starts, provisioned concurrency, concurrency limits and throttling
Platforms compared: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, Google Cloud Run functions; open-source Knative and OpenFaaS
Packaging, dependencies, layers and environment configuration; local emulation and unit testing
Serverless containers and when to choose them over functions

units.title: Managed databases and storage
topics: Object storage: buckets, keys, lifecycle rules, signed URLs, static website hosting
Managed relational databases and serverless SQL; connection pooling from functions
Key-value and document stores: single-table design, partition keys, access patterns, secondary indexes
Consistency, transactions and conditional writes; caching with managed Redis
Choosing a data store for a school results portal, a ride-hailing app and a mobile money ledger

units.title: Event-driven design and queues
topics: Events, commands and messages; event notification, event-carried state transfer and event sourcing
Queues and topics: point-to-point and publish-subscribe; dead-letter queues and visibility timeouts
Streams: partitions, ordering, consumer groups, replay; Kafka and managed streaming services
Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery, idempotent consumers, deduplication, the outbox pattern
Workflows and sagas with step functions and durable orchestration; handling mobile money payment callbacks reliably

units.title: APIs and gateways
topics: API styles: REST, GraphQL, gRPC and webhooks; OpenAPI contracts and versioning
API gateways: routing, request validation, throttling, quotas, caching and custom domains
Authentication and authorisation: JWTs, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, API keys, managed identity providers
Real-time APIs with WebSockets and server-sent events
Backend for frontend and API composition; designing APIs for low-bandwidth mobile clients and USSD gateways

units.title: Observability
topics: The three signals: structured logs, metrics and distributed traces; correlation identifiers
OpenTelemetry instrumentation; tracing a request across functions, queues and databases
Dashboards, service level indicators and alerts for serverless applications
Debugging distributed failures: poison messages, retry storms, timeouts and partial failure
Testing cloud-native applications: contract tests, integration tests in ephemeral environments, chaos experiments

units.title: Designing for cost
topics: Serverless pricing: invocations, duration, memory, requests, data transfer and storage
Comparing the monthly cost of functions, containers and virtual machines at different traffic levels
Cost-aware design: batching, caching, right-sizing memory, avoiding chatty architectures and egress
Budgets, alerts and tagging; a worked estimate in dollars and cedis for a growing start-up

units.title: Deployment and capstone
topics: Infrastructure as code for serverless: SAM, Serverless Framework, Terraform; CI/CD pipelines with staged environments
Security essentials: least-privilege function roles, secrets management, dependency scanning
Data residency considerations when choosing regions for Ghanaian users
Capstone: an event-driven application with functions, a managed database, a queue, an API gateway, tracing and a cost estimate

schedule.title: Cloud-native principles
schedule.exercise: Review a given monolith against the twelve-factor list and write the five changes needed first, with reasons.

tasks.title: Move hard-coded configuration of a sample app into environment variables and verify it runs unchanged in two environments
Choose between monolith, modular monolith, microservices and serverless for three apps and justify using team size, load and cost
Add timeouts, retries with backoff, a circuit breaker and a bulkhead to a client calling a flaky service, and test with 30 percent failures

schedule.title: Functions and the FaaS model
schedule.exercise: Write a note comparing three FaaS platforms for a Ghanaian start-up, covering region, cold start and price.

tasks.title: Create a function with an HTTP trigger, set memory and timeout, invoke it five times and read its logs
Measure cold start latency across 50 invocations, then add provisioned concurrency and compare the median and tail latency
Raise concurrency until throttling occurs, then set limits and a queue so no request is lost during a burst of 500 calls

schedule.title: Packaging and serverless containers
schedule.exercise: Decide whether a given image-resizing service should be a function or a serverless container, and justify.

tasks.title: Write a function with a dependency layer and unit tests that run locally with a mocked event, and show them passing
Package a function with its dependencies and environment settings, deploy it, and fix a missing-dependency failure seen in the logs
Deploy the same service as a function and as a serverless container, compare start time, limits and cost at 100000 monthly requests, and choose

schedule.title: Storage and databases
schedule.exercise: Draw the access patterns of a school results portal and choose a data store for each.

tasks.title: Create a bucket with a lifecycle rule, upload five files, generate a signed URL and verify it expires
Connect a function to a managed SQL database through a connection pool and run 100 concurrent invocations without exhausting connections
Design a single-table key-value layout with partition and sort keys for three access patterns of an orders app and load and query it

schedule.title: Consistency and choosing a data store
schedule.exercise: Justify a data store for a mobile money ledger, a ride-hailing app and a school results portal in a three-row table.

tasks.title: Use a conditional write to prevent two functions overwriting the same record and test with 20 concurrent updates
Add a cache in front of a database, measure the hit rate and stale reads at three TTLs, and select a TTL for a price list
Design the storage for a mobile money ledger with transactions, balances and audit trail, and pass a failure test that kills a function mid-transfer

schedule.title: Events, queues and streams
schedule.exercise: Describe the event flow of an order system, choosing events, commands and queues, and what happens when a consumer fails.

tasks.title: Publish an order event to a topic with two subscribers and show each receives it independently
Set up a queue with a dead-letter queue and visibility timeout, send a poison message and show it moves to the dead-letter queue after 3 tries
Process a partitioned stream with two consumers, show per-key ordering holds, and replay from an earlier offset after a bug

schedule.title: Reliable delivery and workflows
schedule.exercise: Explain why a duplicate mobile money callback must not credit an account twice and how you would prevent it.

tasks.title: Make a consumer idempotent with a deduplication key and verify that 50 duplicate messages change the balance once
Build a payment workflow with steps for validate, charge, notify and compensate, and run it with a failure injected at each step
Implement the outbox pattern so an order record and its event are never out of step, and prove it by crashing between the two writes

schedule.title: APIs, gateways and identity
schedule.exercise: Write an OpenAPI outline for a small bookings API, including versioning and error format.

tasks.title: Define a REST API in an OpenAPI contract with three routes, deploy it, and call each with valid and invalid requests
Configure an API gateway with request validation, throttling at 10 requests per second, a usage quota and a response cache, and verify each limit
Protect an API with a JWT authoriser and scoped permissions, then show that expired, forged and under-scoped tokens are rejected

schedule.title: Real-time and low-bandwidth APIs
schedule.exercise: Design an API for a USSD banking menu and a low-bandwidth mobile app, and list how each keeps payloads small.

tasks.title: Deploy a WebSocket endpoint that broadcasts order status and test it with three connected clients
Compose three backend calls behind one endpoint for a mobile client and measure payload size and latency against the three direct calls
Build a stateless USSD session handler with a menu, session timeout and fallback, and run 20 scripted sessions with correct state

schedule.title: Observability
schedule.exercise: Define three service level indicators and their alert thresholds for a payments API.

tasks.title: Add structured logs with a correlation ID to two functions and follow one request through both logs
Instrument a request across a function, a queue and a database with tracing, and find the slowest span from the trace
Build a dashboard with error rate and latency and an alert on 5 percent errors, then trigger the alert with injected failures

schedule.title: Debugging and testing distributed apps
schedule.exercise: Write a post-incident review of a retry storm that overloaded a database, with timeline, cause and prevention.

tasks.title: Diagnose a queue where one poison message blocks processing, using logs and metrics, and fix it with a dead-letter policy
Write a contract test and an integration test for a function and a queue, and run them against an ephemeral environment
Find and fix a retry storm and a timeout mismatch causing cascading failures in a given system, and prove the fix under load

schedule.title: Serverless cost
schedule.exercise: Prepare a monthly cost estimate in dollars and cedis for a start-up expecting 500000 requests, with three assumptions listed.

tasks.title: Calculate the monthly bill for a function by invocations, duration and memory, and check it against the console estimate
Compare monthly cost of functions, containers and a virtual machine at 10000, 1 million and 100 million requests, and find the crossover points
Reduce the cost of a given design by at least 40 percent using batching, caching, right-sized memory and less data transfer, and show the new estimate

schedule.title: Delivery, security and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write the deployment and rollback plan for the capstone, including who approves each environment.

tasks.title: Describe a function and its API in an infrastructure template, deploy it to dev, and promote it to staging through a pipeline
Reduce a function role to least privilege, move a secret to a secrets manager, and check that an over-privileged call is denied
Build an event-driven app with functions, a managed database, a queue and a gateway, with tracing and a cost estimate, and pass a failure-injection test
